page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute product family. It is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs via multithreading. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally attached, consisting of a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators are present. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance.

Benchmark testing demonstrates standout memory subsystem capabilities and solid computational throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing and large-block memory write bandwidth, which reaches 193.78 GB/sec. Large-block uncached read operations achieve 293.61 GB/sec. Processing evaluations show strong performance in single-core Geekbench (2091.0) and multi-core Geekbench (18542.0), as well as PassMark CPU scores (62405.63). Workload-specific benchmarks indicate top-tier single-threaded compression and text processing, strong Redis operations exceeding 63.9 million operations per second, and PassMark database operation scores of 22098.23.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the instance delivers high resource density for in-memory and data-intensive tasks by pairing dedicated compute threads with generous RAM and local NVMe storage. A performance tradeoff appears in multi-core compute saturation where stress-ng and code compilation scores align closer to median levels, likely influenced by the conservative 2.0 GHz clock speed. This profile is well suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput static web serving, real-time analytics, and data pipeline ETL workloads.
description: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by a dedicated 16-core, 32-thread AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for memory-intensive applications, the configuration features 256.0 GB of system RAM—delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio—paired with 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and no integrated GPUs. Hardware extensions include AVX-512 VNNI, BF16, and cryptographic accelerators. Synthetic and application benchmarks highlight top-tier memory performance, with large-block write bandwidth reaching 193.78 GB/sec and strong database processing exceeding 63.9 million Redis operations per second. While its 2.0 GHz base frequency produces moderate throughput in heavy code compilation and multi-core stress testing, the extensive memory footprint and rapid local NVMe storage offer robust hardware density. The instance is suited for large in-memory caches, relational database systems, ETL processing, and high-concurrency static web workloads.
